Adopt a dark theme by default with a prominent light-mode toggle in the top-right corner. This balances visibility for most users in low-light environments while giving light-sensitive users an immediate escape hatch, cutting cognitive load by making the toggle optional rather than mandatory. The trade-off is that users who prefer light themes will see a brief flash of dark before switching, but this is faster than forcing everyone to choose at setup.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A toggle doesn’t remove the cognitive load—it just moves it from *choosing* a theme to *finding and using* the toggle when glare hits. The real risk is users who need light mode but don’t know it exists until they’re already straining. Settle it with forced-choice testing: give half the users a dark-only interface, half a dark-default with toggle, and measure error rates and recovery time when glare strikes.
